label: Fundamentals & Core Concepts
desc: 16 interview questions covering Fundamentals, LookML, Explores, Dashboards and more.

subs.label: Fundamentals
subs.desc: Looker is a business intelligence (BI) and data visualization platform that lets users explore, analyze, and share data insights, built around a modeling layer (LookML) rather than its own data engine.

subs.label: LookML
subs.desc: LookML's flexibility handles complex data structures by letting you explicitly define relationships, joins, and transformations across files — so even deeply nested or multi-table structures can be modeled as a coherent set of Explores.

subs.label: Explores
subs.desc: A Looker Explore is the interface that lets users interactively explore and analyze data through a graphical, point-and-click UI, built on top of the relationships and fields defined in LookML.

subs.label: Dashboards
subs.desc: A Looker dashboard is a customizable collection of visualizations and reports that gives a consolidated view of key metrics and data insights, typically built from one or more Explores.

subs.label: Ecosystem
subs.desc: Can Looker be integrated with other BI tools or data visualization platforms?

label: LookML, PDTs & Development Workflow
desc: 13 interview questions covering PDTs, LookML, Administration, Visualization and more.

subs.label: PDTs
subs.desc: PDTs are precomputed tables that Looker builds back into the connected database to improve query performance.

subs.label: LookML
subs.desc: What is the purpose of Looker's Liquid syntax in LookML?

subs.label: Administration
subs.desc: Development Mode lets developers change LookML models without affecting the production environment, giving them a safe space to test changes before deploying them live.

subs.label: Visualization
subs.desc: Looker supports custom visualizations built with custom JavaScript or HTML — you can build your own from scratch or adapt third-party visualization libraries for cases the built-in chart types don't cover.

subs.label: SQL Runner
subs.desc: SQL Runner provides a SQL interface directly inside Looker, letting users write and execute custom SQL queries against connected data sources without going through LookML or an Explore.

subs.label: Explores
subs.desc: Dynamic time frame filters let users select relative, time-based periods — such as "last month" or "last year" — that are evaluated dynamically based on the current date, rather than a fixed date range.

subs.label: Version Control
subs.desc: Looker integrates with Git (or other version control systems) so LookML models can be version-controlled like any other codebase.

subs.label: API
subs.desc: The Explore API lets developers programmatically query and retrieve data from Looker Explores, enabling integration with external applications that need Looker-modeled data without going through the UI.

subs.label: Embedding
subs.desc: Explore Embed lets developers embed Looker's Explore functionality directly into external applications, giving end users a full data-exploration experience inside a product they're already using rather than a separate Looker login.

label: Performance, Scale & Data Integration
desc: 21 interview questions covering Performance, Scalability, Data Integration, Real-Time and more.

subs.label: Performance
subs.desc: Looker intelligently caches query results to improve performance, and the caching strategy can be customized based on how frequently and how much the underlying data actually changes.

subs.label: Scalability
subs.desc: Yes — Looker is designed to handle large-scale data processing by leveraging the computing power and scalability of the modern data warehouse or database it's connected to, rather than processing data itself.

subs.label: Data Integration
subs.desc: Looker relies on the underlying data infrastructure to handle incremental data loads — proper configuration and modeling on the warehouse side is required to support incremental updates cleanly.

subs.label: Real-Time
subs.desc: Looker is primarily designed for batch data processing, so it may not be well suited to strictly real-time dashboards.

subs.label: ETL
subs.desc: Can Looker be used for data transformation and ETL processes? How can Looker integrate with data orchestration tools like Apache Airflow?

subs.label: Data Quality
subs.desc: How does Looker handle data quality and cleansing?

label: Governance, Security & Access Control
desc: 13 interview questions covering Security, Compliance, Governance, Access Control and more.

subs.label: Security
subs.desc: Looker offers user access controls, data encryption, and integration with identity providers for authentication and authorization — layering its own permission model on top of whatever security the underlying warehouse already provides.

subs.label: Compliance
subs.desc: Looker provides data encryption, access controls, and features supporting compliance with regulations like GDPR and HIPAA, helping organizations meet industry-specific privacy requirements.

subs.label: Governance
subs.desc: Looker can integrate with external data governance tools through custom scripts, APIs, or data connectors, to enforce governance policies and support compliance beyond what Looker's own controls cover.

subs.label: Access Control
subs.desc: Looker's data permissions and access controls let administrators control which users or groups can access specific data sources, tables, or fields within Looker, down to a fairly granular level.

subs.label: Authentication
subs.desc: Yes — Looker can integrate with external authentication providers such as LDAP, SAML, or OAuth to enable single sign-on (SSO) and centralized user management.

subs.label: Deployment
subs.desc: Can Looker be deployed on-premises or is it only available as a cloud-based solution?

label: Lineage, Collaboration & Platform Administration
desc: 17 interview questions covering Lineage, Administration, Collaboration, Data Actions and more.

subs.label: Lineage
subs.desc: Looker lets you document the logic and definitions of your data models directly in LookML, and provides options to track data lineage and maintain documentation within the platform itself.

subs.label: Administration
subs.desc: Content validation lets users validate the accuracy of data displayed across dashboards, reports, and visualizations — catching broken references (like a renamed field) before they silently break a report.

subs.label: Collaboration
subs.desc: Looker provides features for sharing, commenting, and collaborating on reports, dashboards, and data models, and integrates with communication tools like Slack and email to keep teams in the loop.

subs.label: Data Actions
subs.desc: Data Actions let users take action directly from their data — updating records, creating tasks, or triggering external processes — without leaving the Looker interface.

subs.label: Alerting
subs.desc: Yes — Looker can generate alerts or notifications based on predefined conditions through its scheduling and alerting features, so users are proactively notified when a metric crosses a threshold.

subs.label: Visualization
subs.desc: Yes — Looker supports geospatial data analysis through visualization options including maps and geographic charts.

subs.label: Fundamentals
subs.desc: Can Looker handle data anomaly detection?

subs.label: Governance
subs.desc: Yes — Looker can integrate with data cataloging tools through APIs or connectors, enabling data discovery and cataloging across the organization alongside whatever catalog system is already in use.
